title: Governor of Nebraska

context.text: Incumbent Gov. Jim Pillen (R) is seeking a second term. He won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary with 75.4% of the vote.
Former state Sen. Lynne Walz won the Democratic primary with 91.5%. Rick Beard is the Legal Marijuana NOW nominee.

Former state Sen. Brett Lindstrom, who lost the 2022 Republican primary to Pillen, filed as a nonpartisan candidate but was not qualified: the Secretary of State's office validated 3,358 of 5,765 signatures submitted, and more than 4,000 valid signatures were required. On September 1 he filed instead as the nominee of the America First Party, which the Nebraska Supreme Court had cleared to become an official party the week before. The Secretary of State's final general-election candidate list (September 11) includes the Pillen, Walz, Beard and Lindstrom tickets.
Pillen has said he will not debate; Walz and Beard said they would, and Lindstrom said he would welcome a debate.

candidates.name: Jim Pillen
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. Joe Kelly. Won the May 2026 Republican primary with 75.4%.

summary.text: Jim Pillen is the Republican governor of Nebraska, a veterinarian and livestock producer who served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents before winning the governorship in 2022 with 59.2% of the vote. His office has pursued property-tax changes, and he signed a 12-week abortion limit and a law (LB 574) in 2023 that also restricts gender-altering procedures for people under 19.

background.text: B.S. in animal science from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and D.V.M. from Kansas State University; played defensive back for Nebraska football (1975–1978).
Practicing veterinarian and chair of Pillen Family Farms.
Served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents from 2013 to 2023, including as chair in 2020; elected governor in 2022.

priorities.text: Continue property-tax relief and shrink government spending to give families a break on taxes.
Protect kids, promote Nebraska agriculture and defend Nebraska values, including banning phones in schools and the Stand with Women Act.
priorities.quote: We're going to keep our focus on protecting our kids, promoting Nebraska agriculture, defending Nebraska values, and continuing to lead efforts to fix property taxes in our state.

positions.summary: Signed LB 574 in May 2023, which prohibits abortion when the probable gestational age is twelve or more weeks, with exceptions for medical emergency, sexual assault and incest.

record.text: Signed LB 574 (the Let Them Grow Act and Preborn Child Protection Act), which passed the Legislature 33-15-1 on final reading with an emergency clause; it prohibits abortion at twelve or more weeks gestational age with exceptions, and restricts gender-altering procedures for individuals younger than nineteen.

candidates.name: Lynne Walz
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Ben Steffen, a farmer. Won the May 2026 Democratic primary with 91.5%.

summary.text: Lynne Walz is a former teacher and realtor from Fremont who served in the Nebraska Legislature from 2017 to 2025, including as Education Committee chair, and was the 2018 Democratic lieutenant governor nominee. Her campaign emphasizes property-tax relief that is targeted to working families, public schools, affordability and economic growth.

background.text: Former teacher in Fremont Public Schools and Archbishop Bergan High School; B.A. in elementary education from Midland Lutheran College; current realtor.
Represented District 15 in the Nebraska Legislature from 2017 to 2025 and chaired the Education Committee beginning in 2021.
Ran for lieutenant governor on the 2018 Democratic ticket with Bob Krist.

priorities.text: Targeted tax relief: cut property and other taxes responsibly while keeping vital services, helping working families rather than only top earners.
Grow the economy and rural communities through business growth and investment in broadband, agriculture and small business.
Respect voter-approved measures on issues like medical marijuana, paid sick leave, minimum wage and school vouchers.

candidates.name: Brett Lindstrom
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Mike Picard, a Navy veteran and volleyball club director. Nominee of the America First Party after his nonpartisan petition fell short; listed on the Secretary of State's final general-election candidate list.

summary.text: Brett Lindstrom is a financial adviser and former Republican state senator from Omaha who finished third in the 2022 Republican primary for governor. His platform, the 'Nebraska Doctrine,' focuses on property-tax changes, housing, public power, economic development and artificial intelligence policy.

background.text: B.S. in history from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (2004); walk-on quarterback for the Cornhuskers; has worked as a financial adviser in Omaha.
Represented the 18th District in the Nebraska Legislature from 2015 to 2023; ran in the 2012 Republican primary for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District.
Announced a run for the 2nd District in July 2025 and withdrew in January 2026, then ran for governor as a nonpartisan before filing as the America First nominee.

priorities.text: Property-tax changes, including rolling valuation averaging, cutting the school operating levy cap from $1.05 to 50 cents per $100 of valuation over time, and weighting agricultural land by productive value.
Criticizes the current administration's use of cash reserves and cash funds.
priorities.quote: In three and a half years, this administration has spent through a historic cash reserve, raided cash funds and made billions in commitments with no sustainable way to pay for them.

candidates.name: Rick Beard
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Keenya Barnes, an Omaha Housing Authority commissioner. Nominee of the Legal Marijuana NOW Party.

summary.text: Rick Beard is an Omaha wine professional and private chef running as the Legal Marijuana NOW nominee. His central proposal is a state-run medical cannabis program that he says could generate revenue for property-tax relief.

background.text: Wine professional and private chef; former farmer.

priorities.text: Legalize strong medical cannabis and industrial hemp programs, with a state-run medical cannabis system he estimates could generate $100 million to $500 million a year.
Remove corporate and PAC money from state politics.
Take a more in-depth look at data centers, including a pause on development and mandated closed-loop cooling systems.

positions.summary: Said the state must eliminate tax breaks for corporations and Nebraska’s “ultra-rich.”

researchNotes: The Nebraska Secretary of State's Final Statewide General Candidate List (dated September 11, 2026) lists exactly four Governor/Lt. Governor tickets: Pillen/Kelly (Republican), Walz/Steffen (Democratic), Beard/Barnes (Legal Marijuana NOW) and Lindstrom/Picard (America First); this matches the guide, so Lindstrom is on the ballot as America First. Ballotpedia was unreachable (bot challenge). Pillen's campaign site pages appear partly dated (2022-era issues page); a school-choice position drawn from that page was removed as too vague to map to the issue. Walz's legislative votes (she left the Legislature in January 2025) and Lindstrom's legislative record were not reviewed; our state-legislature snapshot covers only 2026 sessions. Pillen has declined interview/debate requests per news reports. Running mates are listed in each candidate's ballot note.
